objective: Choose the right literal for a value (int, float, str, bool) and explain why some decimal fractions are inexact as floats
secondaryObjectives: Evaluate expressions using arithmetic, string, comparison and Boolean operators with correct precedence and associativity

sources.cite: Python 3.10 documentation (Greek translation, 3.10.22), The Python Tutorial, 15. Floating Point Arithmetic: Issues and Limitations
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the translated page (no current English page appeared in a search). 1/10 has a repeating binary expansion, so any finite number of bits only approximates it; '.1 + .1 + .1 == .3' is False; this is a property of binary floating point, not a bug in Python; rounding after the sum makes comparisons work ('round(.1 + .1 + .1, 10) == round(.3, 10)' is True); the decimal module suits accounting. Storing money as whole cents in an int is the case's fix, a standard practice stated as the author's.

brief.situation: You maintain reconcile.py for Maplewood School District (fictional). Each night it adds up every student lunch account's transactions and freezes any account whose total differs from the stored balance. Last night it froze 312 accounts. A frozen card is refused at the register, and breakfast opens at 07:15. It is 06:25.
handover: Transactions and balances are stored as whole cents (amount_cents, balance_cents) and also shown as dollars (amount, balance).
Last week's change made the script read the dollar fields.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: inspect a flagged account, change the check, run it, unfreeze, or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

scoring.modelReasoning: Every flagged difference is under a cent, which points to representation, not money. 0.10 has no exact binary floating-point value, so 0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 is 0.30000000000000004 and == against 0.30 fails. Money that must be exact belongs in whole cents as ints (or Decimal); the data already has amount_cents and balance_cents. Rounding floats to 2 places passes tonight but keeps money in floats; overwriting balances with float sums corrupts the ledger. A dry run over last night's data proves 0 mismatches before shipping.
